premise: Challenging the undefeated George Foreman in 1974, Ali devised the rope-a-dope strategy to reclaim the world heavyweight championship against overwhelming physical odds.
hook: Every ringside expert thought he was stepping into the ring for a beating, until he leaned against the ropes and absorbed everything Foreman had.
key_facts: Fought George Foreman in Kinshasa, Zaire, on October 30, 1974.
Foreman was undefeated with 40 wins, 37 by knockout.
Ali stayed against the ropes to absorb blows and tire Foreman out.
Won by knockout in the eighth round to reclaim the heavyweight crown.

premise: An advertising illustrator with no film experience pawned personal assets and used an amateur cast to create Pather Panchali, transforming Indian cinema.
hook: He had no prior directing credits, no studio backing, and had to pause filming for months when the money ran out, but his debut ended up winning at Cannes.
key_facts: Worked as a graphic designer for a British advertising agency before filmmaking.
Pawned his wife's jewelry and life insurance to finance early shooting.
Shot 'Pather Panchali' intermittently over nearly three years with an untrained crew.
Won the 'Best Human Document' award at the 1956 Cannes Film Festival.

premise: Keaton risked his life during the filming of Steamboat Bill, Jr. by standing in the exact spot where a real two-ton building wall dropped over him.
hook: A single misplaced step of two inches would have crushed him instantly, yet he insisted on doing the stunt without a double or trick camera.
key_facts: Filmed the climax of 'Steamboat Bill, Jr.' in 1928 during personal and financial distress.
Used a genuine building facade weighing an estimated two tons.
Cleared the falling frame through a single second-story window opening with only inches of tolerance.
Refused a stunt double and performed the sequence in a single continuous take.

premise: Displaced and orphaned during the 1947 Partition, Milkha Singh joined the Indian Army, discovered athletics, and became a record-setting international sprinter.
hook: He arrived in Delhi as a penniless refugee fleeing violence, yet a decade later he was breaking Commonwealth track records.
key_facts: Lost both parents during the Partition of 1947 and fled to Delhi.
Enlisted in the Indian Army's Electrical Mechanical Engineering corps after three failed attempts.
Introduced to organized running while stationed with the Army in 1951.
Won gold in the 400 meters at the 1958 Cardiff Commonwealth Games.

premise: Directing the Manhattan Project to conclusion, Oppenheimer watched the Trinity test detonate and realized the irrevocable shift in human warfare.
hook: The dawn flash in the New Mexico desert turned an academic physicist into the father of an age he subsequently warned the world against.
key_facts: Directed the Los Alamos Laboratory starting in 1943 to develop the atomic bomb.
Oversaw the first successful nuclear detonation at the Trinity site on July 16, 1945.
Recalled thinking of Hindu scripture after the test: 'Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.'
Later lobbied for international regulation of nuclear energy to prevent arms proliferation.

premise: After losing the legal rights to his first hit character, Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, Disney drafted Mickey Mouse on a return train ride, starting a media empire.
hook: He arrived in New York to negotiate a budget raise and left with his lead character stolen and most of his staff poached.
key_facts: Lost the intellectual property rights to 'Oswald the Lucky Rabbit' to distributor Charles Mintz in 1928.
Refused a contract that stripped his creative independence.
Co-created Mickey Mouse alongside animator Ub Iwerks during and after the train ride back to California.
Synchronized sound into 'Steamboat Willie' in 1928, creating a global animation hit.

premise: While stranded in India during World War II, Cambridge-trained physicist Bhabha decided not to return to the West, choosing instead to build India's scientific infrastructure.
hook: Instead of returning to an established European research post, he sent a single letter in 1944 that laid the groundwork for Indian nuclear science.
key_facts: Stranded in India in 1939 due to the outbreak of World War II while on vacation from Cambridge.
Wrote to the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust in 1944 proposing an indigenous research institute.
Founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) in 1945.
Architected India's three-stage nuclear power program.

premise: Barred from American aviation schools due to race and gender, Coleman learned French, traveled abroad, and earned the world's first international pilot license by an African American woman.
hook: Every flight school in the United States slammed the door in her face, so she learned a foreign language at night just to apply overseas.
key_facts: Worked as a manicurist in Chicago while saving money for flight school.
Enrolled in French language classes because American schools rejected her applications.
Trained at the Caudron Brothers' school in Le Crotoy, France.
Earned an international pilot license from the Fédération Aéronautique Internationale in 1921.

premise: Sitting atop an unstable Redstone booster after hours of mechanical delays, Shepard endured intense physiological pressure to become the first American in space.
hook: Strapped into a tiny capsule for four hours while engineers debated sensor glitches, he finally barked over the radio to just fix the problem and light the candle.
key_facts: Selected as one of NASA's original Mercury Seven astronauts in 1959.
Waited over four hours inside Freedom 7 atop the launch pad due to weather and technical checks.
Launched on a 15-minute suborbital flight on May 5, 1961, reaching an altitude of 116 miles.
Became the first American in space, less than a month after Yuri Gagarin's orbital flight.

premise: Torn between international touring as a dancer and mastering classical music, Shankar gave up his glamorous Parisian lifestyle to undergo grueling training under guru Allauddin Khan.
hook: He was already touring the capitals of Europe in custom suits when he gave it all up to shave his head and practice sitar sixteen hours a day in a remote village.
key_facts: Toured Europe as a dancer and musician in his brother Uday Shankar's troupe during the 1930s.
Met multi-instrumentalist Allauddin Khan in 1935 and abandoned stage life to become his disciple.
Moved to the small town of Maihar in 1938 for intensive traditional training.
Introduced Indian classical music to mainstream Western audiences in the 1960s.

premise: Arrested at age eleven and sent to a colored waif's home, Armstrong was handed a cornet that transformed him into one of the founding architects of jazz.
hook: A celebratory gunshot fired into the air on New Year's Eve landed an impoverished New Orleans kid in detention—where he picked up a cornet for the first time.
key_facts: Arrested on December 31, 1912, for firing a pistol into the air to celebrate New Year's.
Sent to the Colored Waif's Home for Boys, where music director Peter Davis taught him the cornet.
Mentored by King Oliver in New Orleans before moving to Chicago in 1922.
Revolutionized jazz phrasing and solo performance with his Hot Five and Hot Seven recordings.

premise: A devastating car crash shattered Cousteau's dream of becoming a naval aviator, forcing him into ocean swimming for rehabilitation and igniting his life's passion.
hook: He was training to be a French naval aviator until a highway wreck broke both arms, sending him into the Mediterranean to rebuild his strength.
key_facts: Graduated from the French Naval Academy and was training as a pilot in 1936.
Suffered a severe car accident that broke both of his arms and ended his aviation career.
Began swimming daily in the Mediterranean Sea to rehabilitate his damaged muscles.
Co-invented the open-circuit underwater breathing apparatus, the Aqua-Lung, with Émile Gagnan in 1943.

premise: Two days before attempting to break the sound barrier, Yeager broke two ribs in a horse-riding accident and used a broom handle to lock the cockpit hatch.
hook: He couldn't even lift his arm to lock the plane's hatch from the inside, so he sneaked a sawed-off broom handle into the cockpit to break the sound barrier.
key_facts: Broke two ribs during a horseback fall two nights before the planned flight in October 1947.
Visited a civilian doctor in town to keep the injury hidden from Air Force medical officers.
Used a ten-inch broomstick lever provided by project engineer Jack Ridley to secure the hatch.
Flew the Bell X-1 past Mach 1 on October 14, 1947, becoming the first person to exceed the speed of sound.

premise: To establish India's space program, Sarabhai chose a quiet fishing village in Kerala and personally convinced the local church community to surrender their cathedral.
hook: Instead of waiting for an industrial complex to be built, he walked into a Sunday church service to ask the parish for their building as a launch facility.
key_facts: Selected Thumba, Kerala, in 1962 because it sat right on the Earth's magnetic equator.
Met the Bishop of Thiruvananthapuram to request St. Mary Magdalene Church as the program's operations base.
The bishop addressed the congregation on Sunday, and the parishioners agreed to relocate.
Launched India's first sounding rocket (Nike-Apache) from the church grounds on November 21, 1963.

premise: One foul away from elimination in the 1936 Olympic long jump trials, Owens was advised by his German rival Luz Long to adjust his takeoff mark, securing his historic gold.
hook: After two straight fouls, his chief German rival walked up, gave him technical advice, and helped him win gold right under Adolf Hitler's gaze.
key_facts: Fouled his first two attempts in the preliminary round of the long jump at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.
German competitor Luz Long suggested he move his takeoff point several inches back from the board to avoid another foul.
Owens qualified easily on his final attempt and won the gold medal with an Olympic record jump of 8.06 meters.
Long was the first to congratulate Owens openly in front of the stadium crowd.
